question: Can a realized terminal funding rate identify the funding information available before settlement?
hypothesis: Many premium histories can map to one terminal rate while their earlier states differ; final rate alone is insufficient to reconstruct ex-ante signal.
falsifier: Fixed counterexample fails, or official evidence explicitly establishes a fixed rate known at the earlier decision time. A current document alone cannot prove historical target applicability.
novelty: Independent information-identification mechanism, not a repeated sum of funding cashflows or beta comparison. Prior work warned realized rates are not signals but did not test prefix identifiability.
baseline: Terminal funding value used retrospectively as a prefix signal
comparison: Three fixed abstract premium paths in basis points [12,-6,0],[-12,6,0],[0,0,0], weights1,2,3; compare first-prefix premium against terminal weighted mean. No calibration or winner.
data_roles: Synthetic identifiability diagnostic and current official documents only; no target market sample or production input. Existing product archival fields reused without raw row rescanning.
source_scope: One targeted official-domain search, then at most two relevant official full pages including current formula or dated formula change. No API or new market downloads.
cost_and_exposure: No trading candidate, exposure or complete cost scenario. Fees, slippage, marks and funding cashflow unknown; actual_net null.
completion: Compute all3 fixed histories, hand checks first, verify official formation/availability rules and identify whether existing three-column settlement files preserve prefix states.
stop: No new paths or historical fitting after source inspection; unknown historical applicability remains unknown.
feedback_disposition: Reuse two current adoption decisions, preserve exact-source/time and unknown-cost boundaries. Existing input-completeness child unchanged. Independent root not feedback offspring.
